title: What If the Y2K Bug Had Never Been Fixed?

scenes.text: What if nobody fixed the Y2K bug? Computers might have read the year 2000 as 1900.
To save costly memory, early programmers stored only the last two digits of the year.
Banks, utilities and government mainframes were most exposed, plus chips in elevators and medical equipment.
Fixing it was not cheap. The research firm Gartner estimated 300 to 600 billion dollars.
When the clocks rolled over, a Senate committee counted over 50 incidents in the U.S. and over 100 elsewhere, all minor.
The bug was real, but the Smithsonian notes it caused no epidemic of failures. Some call that success, others a hoax.

description:
What if the Y2K bug had never been fixed?
Two-digit years put banks, utilities and elevators at risk, and fixing it cost an estimated 300 to 600 billion dollars.
